decisions.reason: The BOM already has a same-message MODIFY requiring the solenoid valve; the CAD integration decision adds no further BOM state change.
A same-message MODIFY already records the solenoid mechanism, dispensing sequence, and controlled flow behavior; CAD integration adds no missing product-state change.
The wiring plan already has a same-message MODIFY requiring solenoid control wiring, so no additional update is necessary.
The CAD integration decision does not alter the existing leak-free plumbing behavior, and the source message's event context is already represented.
The source reiterates that seals must prevent leakage into the base but does not change the existing liquid-isolation requirement.
Integrating the solenoid mechanism into CAD does not change the spout's existing geometry, material, mounting location, or orientation.
The source preserves the existing removable-or-easy-to-clean spout requirement and introduces no necessary change to the dispensing-path state.
A solenoid-based CAD layout does not necessarily replace or modify the existing off-the-shelf electronics strategy.
The dispensing-layout change does not alter the unit's stability or vibration-control requirements.
The CAD integration decision does not change mixing or frothing performance; the source's separate whisk uncertainty is already represented.
The source's splash-control changes already have a same-message MODIFY, while the CAD dispensing integration adds no further splash-state update.
The requirement to depict the solenoid dispensing mechanism in CAD does not necessarily change the established enclosure dimensions or form-factor constraint.
